speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you were involved in a rear-end collision and are now experiencing right groin pain with abnormal leg positioning. Can you tell me exactly how the leg is positioned and if you felt a "pop" or heard a sound at the time of the accident?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right femoral neck fracture. The mechanism of injury (rear-end collision with a restrained driver), immediate onset of severe groin pain, and the patient's age (25) strongly suggest a hip fracture rather than a soft tissue injury. I will request a Hip_X-Ray to confirm the diagnosis.
